moments/m: Adam, an optimizer built on momentum, keeps two running averages for every parameter. The first, m, averages the gradient: each step, m gets beta one times m, plus one minus beta one times the gradient, where beta one, read “beta one”, is the share of m kept.
moments/mnum: Beta one is usually zero point nine. So each step, m keeps nine tenths of itself and takes one tenth of the new gradient.
moments/mom: That looks like momentum's velocity, with two differences: no eta inside, and the gradient is weighted by one minus beta one. So m is not a step: it is an average gradient, in the gradient's own units.
moments/v: The second, v, here not a velocity, averages the squared gradient the same way, keeping a share beta two. It tracks how big this parameter's gradients usually are.
moments/vnum: Beta two is usually zero point nine nine nine: v keeps almost all of itself, and takes a thousandth of each new squared gradient.
start/zero: Both start at zero. After a first gradient of two, m is a tenth of two, zero point two, and v is a thousandth of four, zero point zero zero four. Both are far too small.
start/two: Then the gradient is minus four. m keeps nine tenths of zero point two, zero point one eight, and adds a tenth of minus four: minus zero point two two. v keeps zero point nine nine nine of zero point zero zero four, and adds a thousandth of sixteen: about zero point zero two.
start/steady: Feed m the same gradient, three, step after step, and it levels off at three: nine tenths of three plus a tenth of three is three again. v levels off at nine, the square.
start/flip: Now let the gradient flip between three and minus three. Each push undoes the last inside m, which stays near zero. But every square is nine, so v still heads to nine. m tracks the direction; v tracks the size.
try/p1: Try one: m is zero point five, beta one is zero point nine, and the new gradient is three. What is m after the update?
try/a1: Keep nine tenths of zero point five: zero point four five. Take a tenth of three: zero point three. So m is zero point seven five, a tenth of the way from zero point five toward three.
